summary: A high-performance virtual filesystem (VFS) module that exposes a distributed, erasure-coded object store as a POSIX-compliant filesystem — accessible over NFS, S3, and SMB protocols.
features: Expose a distributed, erasure-coded object store as a POSIX-compliant filesystem
Support for NFS, S3, and SMB protocols
Provide VFS layer for multi-protocol access to the underlying storage system
Create a distributed metadata db instace and expose via vfs
Write files as chunks to the underlying storage with erasure coding
Store and retrieve files with erasure coding for fault tolerance and data durability
interfaces: Programmatic: Go API for VFS operations
UDS: Socket interface for NFS and SMB protocols

summary: A high-performance a user-space NFS (Network File System) server supporting protocols like NFSv3, NFSv4 etc. It is designed to provide a flexible and extensible framework for serving files over the network, with support for various backends and storage systems.
features: Support for NFSv3, NFSv4, and other NFS protocols
User-space implementation for flexibility and extensibility
POSIX-compliant file system access
Support dotfs via FSAL_DOTFS (File System Abstraction Layer)
Communicate with dotfs using sockets
interfaces: TCP/IP: NFS protocol for file sharing over the network

summary: A high-performance SMB/CIFS server implementation that allows file and printer sharing over the network. It is part of the Samba suite and provides support for various SMB protocols, enabling interoperability with Windows clients.
features: Support for SMB1, SMB2, and SMB3 protocols
File and printer sharing over the network
User authentication and access control
Support for various file system features like ACLs, extended attributes
Integration with dotfs for backend storage via vfs_dotfs
Communicate with dotfs using sockets
interfaces: TCP/IP: SMB/CIFS protocol for file and printer sharing

summary: Halmidi is a high-performance, unified Software-Defined Storage (SDS) platform for enterprise unstructured data. It bridges cloud-native object semantics (AWS S3 API) with traditional low-latency POSIX enterprise protocols (NFSv3/v4 via NFS-Ganesha and SMB2/v3 via Samba) over a single shared storage engine without dual-writes, periodic re-indexing, or semantic synchronization gaps
features: Expose a distributed, erasure-coded object store as a POSIX-compliant filesystem
Support for NFS, S3, and SMB protocols
Control plane for managing storage policies, access control, and monitoring
Provide a unified SDS platform for enterprise unstructured data
Bridge cloud-native object semantics with traditional low-latency POSIX enterprise protocols
interfaces: SOAP: RESTful API for AWS S3-compatible object storage
HTTP: RESTful API for management and monitoring

summary: Omashu is a high-performance, distributed metadata database that provides a consistent and fault-tolerant key-value store for managing metadata in a distributed storage system. It is designed to work with dotfs and other storage backends, providing a reliable and scalable solution for metadata management using the Raft consensus algorithm.
features: Distributed key-value store for metadata management
Multi-node deployment with Raft consensus for fault tolerance
Distributed Transactions for atomic operations on metadata
TSO (Timestamp Oracle) for generating globally unique timestamps
etcd/raft for consensus and leader election
BadgerDB for efficient storage and retrieval of metadata
interfaces: Programmatic: Go API for metadata operations
